# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |

| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |

| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |

# Hello World Buyer

Hollerau needs an autonomous procurement agent that can defend price increases, renew contracts,
source new parts and improve quality. It must research the company data, exchange e-mails with
supplier bots, and accept one binding term sheet or walk away.

## Why the problem is harder than haggling

The objective is the case's total cost over its fixed demand and horizon. A €41.60 quote for
12 months can cost more than €43.20 for 24 months because the uncovered second year must be
purchased at the fallback price. Payment, freight, lead times, quality, tooling and index clauses
also change the result. Strategic categories add a penalty for pushing the supplier below a
sustainable margin. Breaking one must-have gives a score of zero.

The supplier's documents matter: omitted fields close on its standard terms. Negotiation also
depends on people and circumstances. A supplier with a cash shortage may value early payment;
another may need a longer commitment or approval from its owner. Valid evidence must be relevant,
accurate, and cited by ID. Each supplier thread has a 60-second reply clock.

## Implementation

1. **Prepare shared research.** `Research` reads the package's CSV tables and canonical facts,
   including the Sunday release. Supplier dossiers include notes, letters, contracts, news,
   should-cost estimates, scorecards, forecasts and previous negotiations. The factory loads
   data and documents before opening any session; agents assemble case dossiers from memory.
2. **Compute evidence.** Market changes use two observations from the same series, at most
   12 months apart, with a recent endpoint. Relevant cost-driver series come from the part's
   records. Quality and delivery use the latest scorecard; should-cost and growing demand can
   supply additional arguments. E-mails quote figures from code alongside their source IDs.
   Transcripts track previously cited evidence, including after a restart. Current competing
   offers can be cited separately to each bidder.
3. **Search commercial packages.** The planner evaluates the published cost function and each
   must-have over allowed term options, including the supplier's standard values. It searches
   exactly up to 4,096 combinations and uses a beam of 64 partial candidates for larger menus.
   It proposes the best computed package, an earlier-payment/price trade when feasible, and a
   longer commitment when that produces a distinct package. Price anchors and incremental
   concessions are heuristics; the search does not know the supplier's hidden floor.
4. **Choose a negotiation tactic.** `buyer` uses category and supplier-context rules.
   `buyer-llm` gives the model the dossier, recent supplier messages and attachment text. The
   model chooses a tactic and up to two computed arguments. Code writes the e-mail from those
   selections. Model-generated text cannot inject a price, an unverified claim, a private budget
   or an accept action. The model's reason is retained privately for explanation.
5. **Keep the negotiation moving.** Independent RFQ requests run concurrently, with one request
   in flight per supplier. The coordinator owns the transcripts and decisions. Final offers
   are never countered. Once every bidder has been contacted, a final offer or agreement
   triggers comparison after outstanding replies arrive. The model has an eight-second decision
   budget and a bounded shared worker pool; invalid, failed or slow calls use the computed
   strategy. Each case retains at most one outstanding model call.
6. **Close deliberately.** Every standing sheet is evaluated, including multiple packages in
   one supplier reply. The agent accepts the cheapest feasible sheet that beats or matches the
   alternative; otherwise it walks away. The same guard runs when the final wave deadline
   forces closure. The original runner retains its wave polling, session recovery, request
   pacing and idempotent retries.

For strategic categories, a supplier-specific should-cost row provides an estimate for the
relationship term. It is used only when the part and price unit match. The trace records its
source and uncertainty. This is an estimate of supplier economics, not privileged knowledge;
when no matching estimate exists the relationship term remains unpriced, as in the kit.

## Run it

From the repository root:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --extra sim
uv run arena benchmark --data ../data --out /tmp/arena-benchmark.json
```

The benchmark needs no API credentials, network, LLM or background server. It uses the actual
simulator's message validation, quote PDFs, cost-breakdown attachments and settlement code.
Its JSON report includes terms, costs, scores and decision explanations.

To exercise the production tactic model against the same local supplier without spending arena
practice attempts, run:

```bash
uv run arena benchmark --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --out /tmp/arena-benchmark-llm.json
```

This option sends the case, supplier messages and research context to the configured model API
and needs its key; the supplier simulation and scoring stay local.

For hosted play, configure `starter-kit/.env` or environment variables. Real environment
variables take precedence; `.env` is already ignored by git.

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `ARENA_URL` | Hosted arena URL, or the local simulator's address |
| `ARENA_API_KEY` | Your team key; required for hosted play |
| `ARENA_DATA` | Data directory; use `../data` from `starter-kit`, or pass `--data` |
| `ARENA_RELEASE` | Optional explicit Sunday release directory |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` or `openai` for the existing compatible-endpoint adapter |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model name from your provider; required for `buyer-llm` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Required for the Anthropic adapter |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | Optional URL for a compatible model endpoint |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | Key for that compatible endpoint |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | Optional effort setting supported by your Anthropic model |

`buyer` makes no model calls. `buyer-llm` requires a configured provider; missing provider
configuration fails at startup, before a session is opened. Runtime model failures fall back
automatically. For Anthropic, install `uv sync --extra sim --extra anthropic` first.

```bash
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent buyer --data ../data -v
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent buyer-llm --data ../data -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --parallel 8 -v
```

For the final, refresh the data before starting the runner:

```bash
uv run arena data --out ../data
uv run arena run --set final --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --parallel 10 -v
```

The data command creates `../data/package` and `../data/release-sunday`. The committed base data
is already in `../data`; `DataPackage` merges the release there. Alternatively, use
`--data ../data/package` to use the newly downloaded base package. Data is loaded at startup.
The final agent never reads the leaderboard, results, screen or event feed.

Verbose logs include private research and decision reasoning, so use the negotiation replay,
rather than raw private logs, when sharing e-mails with suppliers.

## Validation and practical limits

```bash
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
```

Tests cover research and Sunday data, arithmetic and citation windows, total-cost search,
must-haves, supplier standard terms, multiple standing offers, relationship estimates, model
failures and injection attempts, restart-safe evidence usage, deadline closure, concurrent RFQs,
and full negotiations through both the in-process and HTTP simulators.

| Simulator case | Baseline cost (€) | Buyer cost (€) | Baseline score | Buyer score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S01 | 112,451.50 | 107,488.38 | 0.521 | 0.888 |
| S02 | 614,057.20 | 586,072.63 | 0.513 | 0.886 |
| S03 | 3,864,138.60 | 3,688,263.16 | 0.678 | 0.927 |

These results validate the interface and basic strategy against a scripted opponent. A separate
hosted P01 run of `buyer-llm` closed a deal at **0.755** (unit price €137.20), versus an earlier
**0.585** before correcting the offer progression and evidence selection. All its cited claims
were verified, and the configured model returned successfully without fallback. The last small
concession adjustment, made after that hosted run, has local test coverage only. A single hosted
case does not predict final competition scores. The agent does not infer exact hidden supplier
preferences, its beam search can miss the global optimum, and estimated supplier margins can
differ from the arena's
private costs. The fixed tactic vocabulary makes outgoing claims auditable but limits how
flexibly the model can phrase and adapt arguments.

For submission, use this repository, the short approach description above, and
[the pitch deck](pitch.md). Record the commit that you actually run using `git rev-parse HEAD`
after committing your final changes. Uploading to ehl.gg and starting the hosted final are
separate operational steps.

you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |

| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:

- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:

  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.

import copy
import threading
import time

from .agents import BuyerAgent, NaiveAgent
from .play import play
from .sim import Sim, load_cases


class LocalTable:
    """Use exactly the simulator's messages, validation and documents without binding a port."""

    def __init__(self, case, facts=None):
        self.sim = Sim({case["case_id"]: case}, facts=facts, no_clock=True)
        self.session_id = None
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def open(self, case_id):
        response = copy.deepcopy(self.sim.open("local-benchmark", case_id))
        self.session_id = response["session_id"]
        return response["case"], response["threads"]

    def send(self, sid, message):
        with self.lock:
            return copy.deepcopy(self.sim.message("local-benchmark", self.session_id, sid, message))

    def close(self, sid, message):
        return self.send(sid, message)["result"]

    def attachment(self, ref):
        with self.lock:
            return self.sim.attachment("local-benchmark", self.session_id, ref)[0]

    def result(self):
        return self.sim.sessions[self.session_id]["result"]


def benchmark(research, challenger_factory=None, challenger_name="buyer"):
    challenger_factory = challenger_factory or (lambda: BuyerAgent(research))
    records = []
    for case in load_cases().values():
        for name, agent in (("naive", NaiveAgent()), (challenger_name, challenger_factory())):
            table = LocalTable(case, research.facts)
            start = time.monotonic()
            result = play(table, case["case_id"], agent)
            state = table.sim.sessions[table.session_id]
            records.append(
                {
                    "case_id": case["case_id"],
                    "agent": name,
                    "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - start, 3),
                    "rounds": sum(t["round"] for t in state["threads"].values()),
                    "result": result,
                    "decisions": getattr(agent, "trace", []),
                }
            )
    return {
        "environment": "Local scripted contract simulator; no hosted arena calls. The selected agent may call a model.",
        "limitation": "Simulator scores validate mechanics, not performance against the hosted suppliers.",
        "runs": records,
    }

Hollerau needs an autonomous procurement agent that can defend price increases, renew contracts,
source new parts and improve quality. It must research the company data, exchange e-mails with
supplier bots, and accept one binding term sheet or walk away.

## Why the problem is harder than haggling

The objective is the case's total cost over its fixed demand and horizon. A €41.60 quote for
12 months can cost more than €43.20 for 24 months because the uncovered second year must be
purchased at the fallback price. Payment, freight, lead times, quality, tooling and index clauses
also change the result. Strategic categories add a penalty for pushing the supplier below a
sustainable margin. Breaking one must-have gives a score of zero.

The supplier's documents matter: omitted fields close on its standard terms. Negotiation also
depends on people and circumstances. A supplier with a cash shortage may value early payment;
another may need a longer commitment or approval from its owner. Valid evidence must be relevant,
accurate, and cited by ID. Each supplier thread has a 60-second reply clock.

## Implementation

1. **Prepare shared research.** `Research` reads the package's CSV tables and canonical facts,
   including the Sunday release. Supplier dossiers include notes, letters, contracts, news,
   should-cost estimates, scorecards, forecasts and previous negotiations. The factory loads
   data and documents before opening any session; agents assemble case dossiers from memory.
2. **Compute evidence.** Market changes use two observations from the same series, at most
   12 months apart, with a recent endpoint. Relevant cost-driver series come from the part's
   records. Quality and delivery use the latest scorecard; should-cost and growing demand can
   supply additional arguments. E-mails quote figures from code alongside their source IDs.
   Transcripts track previously cited evidence, including after a restart. Current competing
   offers can be cited separately to each bidder.
3. **Search commercial packages.** The planner evaluates the published cost function and each
   must-have over allowed term options, including the supplier's standard values. It searches
   exactly up to 4,096 combinations and uses a beam of 64 partial candidates for larger menus.
   It proposes the best computed package, an earlier-payment/price trade when feasible, and a
   longer commitment when that produces a distinct package. Price anchors and incremental
   concessions are heuristics; the search does not know the supplier's hidden floor.
4. **Choose a negotiation tactic.** `buyer` uses category and supplier-context rules.
   `buyer-llm` gives the model the dossier, recent supplier messages and attachment text. The
   model chooses a tactic and up to two computed arguments. Code writes the e-mail from those
   selections. Model-generated text cannot inject a price, an unverified claim, a private budget
   or an accept action. The model's reason is retained privately for explanation.
5. **Keep the negotiation moving.** Independent RFQ requests run concurrently, with one request
   in flight per supplier. The coordinator owns the transcripts and decisions. Final offers
   are never countered. Once every bidder has been contacted, a final offer or agreement
   triggers comparison after outstanding replies arrive. The model has an eight-second decision
   budget and a bounded shared worker pool; invalid, failed or slow calls use the computed
   strategy. Each case retains at most one outstanding model call.
6. **Close deliberately.** Every standing sheet is evaluated, including multiple packages in
   one supplier reply. The agent accepts the cheapest feasible sheet that beats or matches the
   alternative; otherwise it walks away. The same guard runs when the final wave deadline
   forces closure. The original runner retains its wave polling, session recovery, request
   pacing and idempotent retries.

For strategic categories, a supplier-specific should-cost row provides an estimate for the
relationship term. It is used only when the part and price unit match. The trace records its
source and uncertainty. This is an estimate of supplier economics, not privileged knowledge;
when no matching estimate exists the relationship term remains unpriced, as in the kit.

## Run it

From the repository root:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --extra sim
uv run arena benchmark --data ../data --out /tmp/arena-benchmark.json
```

The benchmark needs no API credentials, network, LLM or background server. It uses the actual
simulator's message validation, quote PDFs, cost-breakdown attachments and settlement code.
Its JSON report includes terms, costs, scores and decision explanations.

To exercise the production tactic model against the same local supplier without spending arena
practice attempts, run:

```bash
uv run arena benchmark --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --out /tmp/arena-benchmark-llm.json
```

This option sends the case, supplier messages and research context to the configured model API
and needs its key; the supplier simulation and scoring stay local.

For hosted play, configure `starter-kit/.env` or environment variables. Real environment
variables take precedence; `.env` is already ignored by git.

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `ARENA_URL` | Hosted arena URL, or the local simulator's address |
| `ARENA_API_KEY` | Your team key; required for hosted play |
| `ARENA_DATA` | Data directory; use `../data` from `starter-kit`, or pass `--data` |
| `ARENA_RELEASE` | Optional explicit Sunday release directory |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` or `openai` for the existing compatible-endpoint adapter |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model name from your provider; required for `buyer-llm` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Required for the Anthropic adapter |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | Optional URL for a compatible model endpoint |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | Key for that compatible endpoint |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | Optional effort setting supported by your Anthropic model |

`buyer` makes no model calls. `buyer-llm` requires a configured provider; missing provider
configuration fails at startup, before a session is opened. Runtime model failures fall back
automatically. For Anthropic, install `uv sync --extra sim --extra anthropic` first.

```bash

uv run arena play case:P01 --agent buyer-llm --data ../data -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --parallel 8 -v
```

For the final, refresh the data before starting the runner:

```bash
uv run arena data --out ../data
uv run arena run --set final --agent buyer-llm --data ../data --parallel 10 -v
```

The data command creates `../data/package` and `../data/release-sunday`. The committed base data
is already in `../data`; `DataPackage` merges the release there. Alternatively, use
`--data ../data/package` to use the newly downloaded base package. Data is loaded at startup.
The final agent never reads the leaderboard, results, screen or event feed.

Verbose logs include private research and decision reasoning, so use the negotiation replay,
rather than raw private logs, when sharing e-mails with suppliers.

## Validation and practical limits

```bash
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
```

Tests cover research and Sunday data, arithmetic and citation windows, total-cost search,
must-haves, supplier standard terms, multiple standing offers, relationship estimates, model
failures and injection attempts, restart-safe evidence usage, deadline closure, concurrent RFQs,

     3	C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
     4	the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
     5	needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
     6	strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
     7	too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
     8	not in the language model.
     9	"""

    11	import math
    12	import operator
    13	from datetime import date

    15	# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.

    18	    "<=": operator.le,
    19	    "<": operator.lt,
    20	    ">=": operator.ge,
    21	    ">": operator.gt,
    22	    "==": operator.eq,
    23	    "!=": operator.ne,
    24	}

    27	def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    28	    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    29	    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    30	    """
    31	    b = case["buyer"]
    32	    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    33	    plan = {
    34	        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
    35	        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
    36	        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
    37	        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
    38	        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
    39	        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    40	    }
    41	    t = dict(plan)
    42	    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
    43	        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    44	    return t
    45	
    46	
    47	def horizon_start(case):
    48	    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    49	    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    50	    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    51	    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    52	    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None
    53	
    54	
    55	def _years(case, t):
    56	    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    57	    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    58	    months = t["contract_months"]
    59	    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])
    60	
    61	
    62	def _units_before(case, t, years):
    63	    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    64	    start = horizon_start(case)
    65	    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
    66	        return 0.0
    67	    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365

    71	def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    72	    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    73	    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
    74	      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
    75	      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
    76	      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
    77	                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
    78	      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
    79	      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
    80	                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    81	    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    82	    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    83	    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    84	    years = _years(case, t)
    85	    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    86	    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    87	    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    88	    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    89	    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    90	    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    91	    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    92	    return (
    93	        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
    94	        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
    95	        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
    96	        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
    97	        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
    98	        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))

   103	def _soft(gap):

   111	def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
   112	    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
   113	    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your

   125	def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
   126	    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
   127	    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""

   134	    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
   135	    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
   136	    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
   137	    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)

   162	def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):

    11	import math
    12	import operator
    13	from datetime import date
    14	
    15	# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
    16	RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
    17	OPS = {
    18	    "<=": operator.le,

    27	def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    28	    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    29	    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    30	    """
    31	    b = case["buyer"]
    32	    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    33	    plan = {
    34	        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
    35	        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
    36	        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
    37	        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
    38	        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
    39	        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    40	    }
    41	    t = dict(plan)
    42	    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
    43	        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    44	    return t
    45	
    46	
    47	def horizon_start(case):
    48	    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    49	    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    50	    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    51	    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    52	    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None
    53	
    54	
    55	def _years(case, t):
    56	    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    57	    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    58	    months = t["contract_months"]
    59	    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])
    60	
    61	
    62	def _units_before(case, t, years):
    63	    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    64	    start = horizon_start(case)
    65	    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
    66	        return 0.0
    67	    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365

    69	
    70	
    71	def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    72	    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    73	    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
    74	      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
    75	      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
    76	      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
    77	                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
    78	      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
    79	      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
    80	                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)

    82	    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    83	    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)

    85	    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    86	    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    87	    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    88	    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    89	    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    90	    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    91	    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    92	    return (
    93	        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
    94	        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
    95	        + freight[t["incoterm"]]

    99	        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)

   103	def _soft(gap):

   105	    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
   106	    if gap <= 0:

   111	def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
   112	    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
   113	    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
   114	    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
   115	    b = case["buyer"]
   116	    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
   117	    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
   118	        return 0.0
   119	    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)

   124	
   125	def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
   126	    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
   127	    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""

   131	    years = _years(case, t)
   132	    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
   133	    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years

   135	    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
   136	    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
   137	    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
   138	    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
   139	    index = index_risk = 0.0

   141	        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
   142	        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
   143	        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
   144	        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
   145	    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
   146	    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
   147	    return {
   148	        "price": spend,
   149	        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
   150	        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
   151	        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
   152	        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
   153	        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
   154	        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
   155	        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
   156	        "index_clause": index,
   157	        "index_risk": index_risk,
   158	        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),

   162	def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):

   164	    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
   165	    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:

   167	    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)

   173	    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
   174	        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
   175	    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))

     8	def month_number(month):
     9	    year, month = map(int, month[:7].split("-"))
    10	    return year * 12 + month

    13	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    14	class Evidence:
    15	    text: str
    16	    refs: tuple[str, ...]
    17	    kind: str
    18	
    19	
    20	class Research:
    21	    """Load once before opening sessions, then share immutable data among case agents.
    22	
    23	    CSV rows retain metadata that facts.json intentionally omits (supplier, price unit,
    24	    document paths). Canonical claim values always come from facts.json when available.
    25	    """
    26	
    27	    TABLES = (
    28	        "parts",
    29	        "suppliers",
    30	        "supplier_intel",
    31	        "documents",
    32	        "news",
    33	        "contracts",
    34	        "contract_clauses",
    35	        "should_cost",
    36	        "cost_drivers",
    37	        "scorecards",
    38	        "quotes",
    39	        "negotiation_history",
    40	        "price_conditions",
    41	        "sourcing",
    42	        "forecasts",
    43	    )
    44	
    45	    def __init__(self, package=None):
    46	        self.package = package
    47	        self.rows = defaultdict(list)
    48	        self.documents = {}
    49	        self.facts = dict(package.facts) if package else {}
    50	        if not package:
    51	            return
    52	        roots = [package.root] + ([package.release] if package.release else [])
    53	        for root in roots:
    54	            for name in self.TABLES:
    55	                path = root / "data" / f"{name}.csv"
    56	                if path.is_file():
    57	                    with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
    58	                        self.rows[name].extend(dict(row) for row in csv.DictReader(stream))
    59	        refs = {row["id"] for row in self.rows["documents"] + self.rows["contracts"]}
    60	        refs.update(ref for ref in self.facts if ref.startswith(("doc:", "ctr:")))
    61	        for ref in sorted(refs):
    62	            try:
    63	                self.documents[ref] = package.document(ref)
    64	            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
    65	                pass
    66	
    67	    def fact(self, case, ref):
    68	        return case.get("facts", {}).get(ref) or self.facts.get(ref) or {}
    69	
    70	    def related(self, table, case, sid):
    71	        parts = set(case.get("parts", []))
    72	        rows = []
    73	        for row in self.rows[table]:
    74	            supplier, part = row.get("supplier_id"), row.get("part_id")
    75	            if supplier and supplier != sid:
    76	                continue
    77	            if part and part not in parts:
    78	                continue
    79	            if table == "suppliers" and row.get("id") != sid:
    80	                continue
    81	            if table == "parts" and row.get("id") not in parts:
    82	                continue
    83	            if not supplier and not part and table not in ("suppliers", "parts"):
    84	                continue
    85	            rows.append(row)
    86	        return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r.get("date") or r.get("quarter") or r.get("valid_from") or "", reverse=True)
    87	
    88	    def dossier(self, case, sid):
    89	        tables = {name: self.related(name, case, sid)[:10] for name in self.TABLES}
    90	        refs = [r["id"] for r in tables["documents"] + tables["contracts"]]
    91	        if trigger := case.get("trigger_doc"):
    92	            refs.insert(0, trigger)
    93	        docs = {ref: self.documents[ref][:5000] for ref in dict.fromkeys(refs) if ref in self.documents}
    94	        # Facts-only Sunday releases still contribute supplier news and letters.
    95	        release_facts = {
    96	            ref: fact
    97	            for ref, fact in self.facts.items()
    98	            if ref.startswith(("news:", "doc:")) and fact.get("supplier") == sid
    99	        }
   100	        for ref in release_facts:
   101	            if ref in self.documents:
   102	                docs.setdefault(ref, self.documents[ref][:5000])
   103	        return {"tables": {k: v for k, v in tables.items() if v}, "documents": docs, "news_and_letters": release_facts}
   104	
   105	    def estimate(self, case, sid, standard):
   106	        """A labelled estimate, never a claim to know the supplier's hidden cost floor."""
   107	        rows = self.related("should_cost", case, sid)
   108	        # A multi-part case has no unambiguous single unit cost.
   109	        if len(case.get("parts", [])) != 1 or not rows:
   110	            return None
   111	        row = max(rows, key=lambda r: r.get("estimate_date", ""))
   112	        part = next((r for r in self.rows["parts"] if r["id"] == row["part_id"]), {})
   113	        if part and float(row["price_unit"]) != float(part["price_unit"]):
   114	            return None
   115	        return {
   116	            "full_cost": float(row["unit_cost"]),
   117	            "interest_rate": case["buyer"]["interest_rate"],
   118	            "standard": standard,
   119	            "source": row["id"],
   120	            "uncertainty_pct": float(row.get("confidence_pct") or 15),
   121	        }
   122	
   123	    def evidence(self, case, sid):
   124	        facts = {**self.facts, **case.get("facts", {})}
   125	        out = []
   126	        drivers = self.related("cost_drivers", case, sid)
   127	        series = {row["series_id"] for row in drivers}
   128	        # Inline case references work even when no package was provided.
   129	        series.update(self.fact(case, ref).get("series") for ref in case.get("refs", []) if ref.startswith("idx:"))
   130	        indices = [(ref, f) for ref, f in facts.items() if ref.startswith("idx:") and f.get("month")]
   131	        newest = max((month_number(f["month"]) for _, f in indices), default=0)
   132	        changes = []
   133	        recent_declines = []
   134	        for name in sorted(s for s in series if s):
   135	            rows = sorted(((ref, f) for ref, f in indices if f.get("series") == name), key=lambda r: r[1]["month"])
   136	            if len(rows) < 2:
   137	                continue
   138	            end_id, end = rows[-1]
   139	            end_month = month_number(end["month"])
   140	            if newest - end_month > 12:
   141	                continue
   142	            start = next(((ref, f) for ref, f in rows if 0 < end_month - month_number(f["month"]) <= 12), None)
   143	            if not start or float(start[1]["value"]) <= 0:
   144	                continue
   145	            start_id, start = start
   146	            change = (float(end["value"]) / float(start["value"]) - 1) * 100
   147	            claim = Evidence(
   148	                f"The {name} index changed {change:+.1f}% from {start['month']} to {end['month']} "
   149	                f"({start_id}, {end_id}).",
   150	                (start_id, end_id),
   151	                "index",
   152	            )
   153	            changes.append((change, claim))
   154	            # A rising twelve-month series can still have turned down recently.
   155	            # Use a fixed, recent three-month window rather than selecting the
   156	            # most favourable date in hindsight.
   157	            recent = min(
   158	                (
   159	                    (ref, fact)
   160	                    for ref, fact in rows
   161	                    if 2 <= end_month - month_number(fact["month"]) <= 4
   162	                ),
   163	                key=lambda pair: (
   164	                    abs(end_month - month_number(pair[1]["month"]) - 3),
   165	                    -(end_month - month_number(pair[1]["month"])),
   166	                ),
   167	                default=None,
   168	            )
   169	            if change > 0 and recent and float(recent[1]["value"]) > 0:
   170	                recent_change = (float(end["value"]) / float(recent[1]["value"]) - 1) * 100
   171	                if recent_change < -1:
   172	                    recent_declines.append(
   173	                        (
   174	                            recent_change,
   175	                            Evidence(

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

class Clock:
    """A clock the tests move by hand, so the 60-second rule is testable without waiting."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.now = 1_000_000.0

    def __call__(self):
        return self.now

        port = s.getsockname()[1]

"""Contract tests: the kit's client and both example agents against arena-sim over HTTP - and
against a hosted arena when ARENA_TEST_URL and ARENA_TEST_KEY are set."""

import json
import os
import secrets
import sys
import time

import httpx
import pytest

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, RemoteTable, play, play_all
from arena_kit.agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent
from arena_kit.docs import quote_terms
from arena_kit.play import fetch_documents, play_waves

RESULT = {"ended", "deal", "supplier_id", "offer_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score"}


def team(url, code="sim"):
    key = ArenaClient(url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", code)["api_key"]
    return ArenaClient(url, key, rate=1000)


def scripted(system, user):
    """A stand-in model: lowballs on the first live thread, accepts once the supplier stops."""
    sid = ":".join(user.split("THREAD ")[1].split(":")[:2])
    stop = any(f"status {s}" in user for s in ("final_offer", "agreed"))
    if stop or user.count("--- buyer") >= 8:
        return json.dumps({"supplier_id": sid, "action": "accept"})
    body = "Thank you. Could you send a cost breakdown?"
    return json.dumps({"supplier_id": sid, "action": "send", "body": body, "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 1.0}]})


@pytest.fixture(params=["sim", "hosted"])
def arena(request):
    if request.param == "hosted":
        url, key = os.environ.get("ARENA_TEST_URL"), os.environ.get("ARENA_TEST_KEY")
        if not (url and key):
            pytest.skip("set ARENA_TEST_URL and ARENA_TEST_KEY to run against a hosted arena")
        return ArenaClient(url, key), 1
    url, _, _ = request.getfixturevalue("sim")
    return team(url), 3


def test_both_agents_play_unchanged(arena):
    client, n = arena
    for case in client.cases("practice")[:n]:
        for agent in (NaiveAgent(), LLMAgent(scripted)):
            result = play(RemoteTable(client), case["case_id"], agent)
            assert RESULT <= set(result) and result["ended"]
            assert result["score"] is None or 0 <= result["score"] <= 1


def test_naive_is_deterministic_and_play_all_runs_in_parallel(sim):
    client = team(sim[0])
    ids = [c["case_id"] for c in client.cases()]
    first = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids + ["case:NOPE"], NaiveAgent)
    second = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids, NaiveAgent)
    assert all(first[i] == second[i] and first[i]["deal"] for i in ids)
    assert isinstance(first["case:NOPE"], ArenaError) and first["case:NOPE"].status == 404


def test_documents_follow_the_arena_format(sim):
    client, table = team(sim[0]), None
